sentences.text: Bolong was a relatively small dinosaur measuring about 4 meters long and weighing 200 kilograms. It possessed a convex, stocky head equipped with powerful mandibles and relatively large teeth.

The holotype specimen, YHZ-001, is a nearly complete skeleton that forms the basis of the species description. A second specimen, ZMNH-M8812, an almost complete skeleton of a juvenile, was found by a farmer near Xitaizhi in Inner Mongolia in 2013.

Bolong is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of western Liaoning Province, China. The genus name Bolong honors the brothers Bo Hai-chen and Bo Xue, who assisted in its discovery, and the Chinese word for dragon. The genus Bolong was named by Wu Wen-hao, Pascal Godefroit, and Hu Dong-yu in 2010.

The gait of Bolong is debated; its short forelimbs with unfused wrist bones suggest they were not well-adapted for weight-bearing, despite proportions reminiscent of quadrupeds. Bolong's short and robust hind foot resembles that of fully quadrupedal dinosaurs rather than bipedal ones. Very young Bolong individuals had proportionally longer forelimbs, typical of quadrupedal animals.

Bolong is classified within Hadrosauroidea and is considered one of the most basal hadrosauroids found in Asia. Bolong belongs to the family Iguanodontidae. Bolong is a member of the class Ornithischia.
Bolong lived approximately 125 million years ago during the earliest Barremian stage. Bolong lived from the Barremian to the Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
